issues.detail: The Greek 'λεγει' (says) is part of the narrative sequence describing what happened when the firstborn was brought into the world. The Vietnamese translation 'phán rằng' (said that/proclaimed) implies a direct speech or a command issued by the firstborn, which is not present in the Greek text.

The Greek verb 'προσκυνησατωσαν' is an aorist indicative, indicating a completed action (they worshiped). The Vietnamese translation 'phải thờ lạy' uses the modal 'phải' (must/have to), changing the meaning from a statement of fact about what happened to a command or obligation.
